topic: adaptive neural inference; early exit; confidence calibration; latency/accuracy trade-offs
status: cross-paper objective interaction; matched modern evaluation open
claim: A 2018 flexible-ensemble study reports a favorable ImageNet AlexNet point (7-model runtime 11.67→6.51 ms, top-1 accuracy .6043→.6032) using score-margin-based early stopping with training-set threshold search. A separate 2020 edge-offloading study finds miscalibrated exit confidence can violate target accuracy, and temperature scaling improves target reliability; however, at a low target accuracy of .75 the uncalibrated policy may have lower missed-deadline probability because it offloads more. Together these papers support an objective-conditional conclusion: confidence-driven adaptive computation must be evaluated against both accuracy and service latency/deadline targets, and calibration may trade off those outcomes rather than uniformly dominate.

sources.title: Calibration-Aided Edge Inference Offloading via Adaptive Model Partitioning of Deep Neural Networks
locators: §IV-E: at target .75, conventional policy can have lower missed-deadline probability

interpretation: These are different adaptive-inference policies, datasets, model families, hardware/timing methods, and objectives; the figures are not a direct comparative effect estimate. The 2018 result is a useful within-study point, not a guarantee of zero accuracy loss. The 2020 low-target result is a countercondition to the claim that calibration always improves end-to-end service.
falsifiable_question: On matched modern models and hardware, does calibrating confidence thresholds reduce target-accuracy outage without increasing deadline misses across in-distribution and shifted data, and how does the answer vary with target accuracy, latency budget, and offload cost?
primary_outcome: Jointly report accuracy, tail/mean latency, energy, early-exit/offload fraction, target-accuracy outage, and deadline-miss probability across thresholds and shifts.
counterevidence_and_caveats: The 2018 AlexNet point shows nearly 2× runtime reduction with a very small reported accuracy decrease on the evaluated ImageNet setup.
The 2020 study shows calibration can improve accuracy reliability yet be worse on the deadline objective at target .75.
The 2018 thresholds are optimized on training data and use a selected α=.5 weighted objective.
The 2020 study uses one CIFAR-10/AlexNet-style split, batch-level metrics, and partly estimated device/cloud runtimes.
Neither study establishes current accelerator performance or robustness under distribution shift.
suggested_design: Choose one shared set of early-exit models, datasets, and hardware; compare raw confidence, temperature-scaled confidence, and adaptive difficulty-aware thresholds with identical calibration data and compute budgets. Tune only on validation data, evaluate multiple target accuracies and network delays, include distribution shifts, and report paired per-example exits plus both deadline and outage outcomes.

topic: probability of causation; mediation; partial identification
status: cross-era theorem/example synthesis; assumptions and version chronology require care
claim: Across the sampled mediation analysis and two follow-ups, information about a mediator does not uniformly sharpen an individual probability-of-causation interval. Under the 2014 text's binary complete-mediation/no-direct-effect/no-confounding assumptions, the mediator leaves the lower bound unchanged but can improve a vacuous upper bound (worked example .60–1 to .60–.76). The 2017 partial-mediation paper provides a counterexample where mediator use widens the upper bound (.88 to .95) and recommends taking the tighter of the mediator-aware and mediator-ignorant bounds. A 2022 journal treatment generalizes complete mediation to binary causal chains but still characterizes the gains as modest and asymmetric under its idealized known-chain assumptions.

Scope excludes direct X→Y effects in its idealized chain analysis

interpretation: This is a bounded mathematical synthesis, not a new estimator or evidence that mechanism data are generally harmful. A tighter interval still does not identify the individual counterfactual unless assumptions/data suffice; the estimand is causes-of-observed-effects, not the population average treatment effect.
falsifiable_question: When the causal graph has partial mediation, direct effects, confounding, or mediator measurement error, when does adding mediator evidence reduce versus widen a valid probability-of-causation interval, and can a predeclared rule that also reports the mediator-ignorant bound guarantee non-worsening coverage?
primary_outcome: Coverage and width of identified intervals against known counterfactual ground truth in simulations, with sensitivity analysis for direct effects, confounding, and measurement error; separately report identification frequency.
counterevidence_and_caveats: Complete mediation under the stated assumptions can improve the upper bound and never worsen the cited bound.
Partial mediation may improve or worsen the upper bound; in the cited example it is wider, so authors recommend comparing both bounds.
The 2022 complete-chain study finds some cases of identification and positive gains, not zero utility.
Strong no-confounding/structural assumptions and binary variables restrict transfer; partial mediation requires additional conditions.
The 1411.2636 frame date is 2014, but the PDF served at its v1 URL has a February 2022 body date; do not use it as pre-2015 evidence without resolving source chronology.
suggested_design: Generate potential-outcome simulations with known individual truth under complete/partial mediation, direct effects, confounding, and noisy/missing mediators. Compare outcome-only, mediator-aware, and minimum-upper-bound strategies; assess coverage, interval width, and assumption sensitivity, then replicate in one domain with a defensible causal graph.
